MetricPage.indexMetaDescription: Every measure we show, what it counts, and whether it applies to skills, roles or both.
MetricPage.indexLede: Every measure has one definition, one denominator and one source. Only valid combinations appear in the app — an industry has no salary figure, so we never show one.
MetricPage.legendText: Read from ad text — has a known error rate

tierNote.common: Shown on boards and ticker pages. Start here.
tierNote.advanced: Behind “More measures”. Noisier or easier to misread — read the definition before leaning on one.

MetricPage.indexFooter: How the underlying data is collected, and what we never collect:
MetricPage.factWindowValue: {days} days, ending with the latest complete week
MetricPage.factSample: At least {min} ads, otherwise we say “not enough ads” and draw nothing
MetricPage.factHistoryValue: {days} days of tracking for an item
MetricPage.factHistoryNone: Available from the first day we track an item
MetricPage.textBody: This measure comes from rules applied to the wording of each ad. Rules miss some phrasing and misread some ads — the known error from our hand-checked sample is in “Known limits”, and the rules themselves are on the sources page.
MetricPage.exNote: Across Australia, all levels, this week.

signalUse.change_4w: This is the signal measure. We flag “more ads” when it is at least +{rel}% and at least {abs} more ads, and “fewer ads” for the same size of fall — only when there are at least {min} ads behind it.
signalUse.entry_level_share: We flag “more entry-level openings” when this share rises by at least {pp} percentage points compared with eight weeks earlier, with at least {min} ads behind it.
signalUse.growth_12m: Shown next to roles in lists for context. It does not trigger alerts: official series are revised, and a year is too slow to act on.
signalUse.none: Not used for signals. It’s here to give context next to demand, not to tell you when to act.

SourcesPage.metaDescription: Where our numbers come from, how filters become numbers, the sample threshold, extraction rules and their known error, and what we never collect.
SourcesPage.title: Sources and method
SourcesPage.lede: Every number in the app traces back to a licensed source, a collection time and a count of ads. This page is the long version of every ⓘ.
SourcesPage.illustrativeMore: The method below is the one the live pipeline uses.

use.ads: Skill-level counts, entry-level share, work rights, work mode and advertised pay.
use.official: Occupation-level demand for roles, including the 12-month change.
use.practitioner: What people in the work said after coffee chats — only ever shown in aggregate.

status.delayed: Running late — numbers may be a day old
status.failed: Last run failed — showing the previous run

SourcesPage.kindsLede: Next to every number is a small mark for the kind of source it comes from. The shape carries the meaning, so it still works without colour.

kindBody.official: Published by government agencies such as Jobs and Skills Australia. Counted at occupation level, revised from time to time, and slower to move.
kindBody.ads: Counts from licensed job-ad data, collected daily. Fast and skill-level, but ads are not the same as jobs: some are duplicates, some are never filled.
kindBody.practitioner: Experience from verified practitioners after coffee chats. It’s personal and qualitative — never a statistic about a market.

SourcesPage.cells1: When we collect an ad we file it into exactly one cell, made of four things:

cellHint.place: The most specific region we can tell, e.g. Parramatta rather than Sydney
cellHint.mode: On-site, hybrid or remote. Ads that don’t say count as on-site
cellHint.level: Graduate, other entry-level, or everything else
cellHint.rights: Requires PR or citizenship, not stated, or sponsorship offered

SourcesPage.cells2: Your filter is turned into the set of cells it covers. Places expand to everything inside them, and rules are combined so that an ad matching two rules is still counted once.
SourcesPage.cellsExample: “On-site in Sydney or Melbourne, plus remote anywhere in Australia” covers every Sydney and Melbourne region for on-site ads, and every Australian region for remote ads — added up once each.
SourcesPage.cells3: Shares use the same cells for the top and the bottom of the fraction, so a percentage always means “of ads matching your filter”. A few shares deliberately ignore one filter — entry-level share ignores the level filter, for example — and say so in their definition.
SourcesPage.sampleTitle: At least {min} ads, or no number
SourcesPage.sample1: If fewer than {min} ads sit behind a number, we show “not enough ads” instead of a value, draw no trend line and raise no signal. We suggest how to widen the filter instead.
SourcesPage.sample2: Salary comparisons need more: the skill premium needs at least {premium} ads that state a salary.
SourcesPage.textLede: Some measures depend on how an ad is worded. We use written rules, test them on a hand-checked sample of ads, and publish the known error next to each one.
SourcesPage.noKnownError: Being measured on our hand-checked sample.
SourcesPage.textFoot: Rules are versioned. When a rule changes, we re-run it over past ads so trends don’t jump because of our own change.

signalRule.rise: Ads in the last four weeks are at least {rel}% and at least {abs} ads higher than the four weeks before, with at least {min} ads behind it.
signalRule.fall: The same test in the other direction: at least {rel}% and {abs} ads lower. Worded neutrally — a fall is information, not a warning.
signalRule.entry_open: The share of entry-level ads is at least {pp} percentage points higher than eight weeks earlier, with at least {min} ads behind it.

SourcesPage.signalsFoot: Signals describe the market. They never rank people and never tell you what to learn.

never.n1: We never scrape LinkedIn, SEEK or any site whose terms forbid it. Job-ad data comes from licensed APIs and published statistics only.
never.n2: We never buy or build profiles of individual job seekers, and we never sell data. No one can pay to change what the market shows, and any conflict of interest is disclosed.
never.n3: We never show practitioner feedback about an individual — only aggregated, with enough responses to protect identities.

SourcesPage.neverFoot: Personal data is stored in Australia, in line with the Privacy Act 1988 and the Australian Privacy Principles.
